text: The Crimson Elite Raider, also known as the Advanced Elite Raider, is an uprated variant of the Cylon Raider fighter craft. This fighter is piloted by Crimson Elite class Cylons and appears to be a prototype. Some versions of the Elite Raider are equipped with a cloaking device. Faster and better armored than the standard Raider, it is armed with two forward firing energy weapons. The vessel's design merges elements of both the Original Series Raider and the more streamlined Raider from the 2003 Miniseries (2003 Video Game).

Formally, the "conn" of a Colonial Fleet warship is the collective name for its helm controls: yaw, pitch, and roll. The term is also used to grant command of a ship from a commanding officer to a subordinate, typically an Executive officer. After placing Pegasus in a precarious situation that required his engineering leadership to save the ship, Commander Barry Garner tells Major , "You have the conn" .

Connor may refer to one of the following: * Charlie Connor, a New Caprica Resistance fighter, former member of the Circle and barkeep at Joe's bar. * Kevin Connor, the son of Charlie Connor, killed by the Cylons during the temple raids on New Caprica. * Connor Widdows, the actor who played Boxey in the Re-Imagined Series. * Keegan Connor Tracy, the actress who portrays Jeanne, a member of the Cult of Baltar. * You may also be looking for Conoy, as in Leoben Conoy, the humanoid Cylon first encountered on Ragnar Anchorage in the Miniseries.

The Communications Officer manages the main communications aboard a typical Colonial Forces ship. A communications officer's typical responsibilities include: * Monitoring communications of a ship's incoming and out-going communications * Monitoring fleet-wide communications from the command battlestar of a battlestar group or other fleet * Ensuring all communications are properly logged * Relaying communications to a battlestar's s and Raptors during off-ship missions * Managing other minor CIC operations in the absence of the Senior Officer of the Watch Anastasia Dualla and Lieutenant Louis Hoshi are both communication officers. Petty Officer Sian fills in for Dualla during the episode "Sacrifice". de:Kommunikationsoffizier

During the First Cylon War, Cylons use ground vehicles in ground assaults of urban population centers and planetary facilities, escorted by Cylon Centurions. The Cratus is a brand new ship design introduced into the first downloadable content (DLC) of the second season titled: "Resurrection".

The Cylon assault ship is a formidable, new type of Cylon warship commanded by the Imperious Leader. It is deployed to engage a Colonial Viper squadron that is harassing a Cylon task force. The vessel proves difficult for the Vipers to damage. Its unique offensive capability involves discharging liquid tylium from its exhaust ports, which then ignites, creating a massive fireball that destroys at least one Viper. The ship is ultimately destroyed when Apollo fires a missile containing a modified impulse microvator into it, causing a chain reaction .

Deck Crew 5 was the name given to the deck crew attached to , formerly a part of Battlestar Group 75, and responsible for maintenance of the battlestar's craft, such as s and Raptors. At the time of the Cylon Attack, Deck Crew 5 included: * Chief Petty Officer Galen Tyrol * Specialist Socinus * Specialist Prosna * Specialist Cally Tyrol (née Henderson)

following the use of the electric pulse generators .]] An electromagnetic pulse (EMP) generator is an anti-electronics weapon that mimics the intense EM radiation created by a nuclear explosion in an atmosphere. The resulting EM field couples with nearby electronics systems, inducing electrical currents and voltages, thus damaging sensitive electronic equipment. Pulse generators are able to act independently, at some level, without needing to be connected to a ship's power grid. They may be an offshoot of, or connected to, FTL technology due to its employment of hyperspace principles .

The Eastern Alliance destroyer is a spacecraft used by the Eastern Alliance of Terra. An Eastern Alliance destroyer tracks the Lunar Avion from Lunar Seven to Paradeen where it eventually encounters the . Commandant Leiter commands the destroyer that is captured by the Colonials. Lanceman and Donner are crewmen aboard the destroyer . The destroyer manages to escape from Galactica, and returns to Terra with the Colonials on its trail . The Eastern Alliance destroyer was repeatedly noted to be far smaller that a battlestar and non-threatening as a contender. In fact, a captured destroyer was briefly impounded aboard Galactica and appeared to be comparable in size to a Colonial shuttle. However, Commandant Leiter confidently boasts to Commander that many of these destroyers could take on Galactica like a wolf pack takes on its prey , though this has never been proved nor disproved. After Leiter's destroyer escapes, a Viper squadron is dispatched to pursue the destroyer. However, the conclusion of the war between the Eastern Alliance and the Terran Nationalists presumably rendered both the Viper squadron's mission, and the mission of the destroyer itself, unnecessary .

A deltoid spanner is a tool used in the maintenance of a space ship. In an alternate scene where approaches Robber, the latter asks for and receives this tool from Starbuck (deleted scene, The Long Patrol).

The derelict mothership is a ship of unknown origin encountered by . It is detected around the same time Commander experiences his nightmare, which consists of the entire Fleet being destroyed by an unknown cosmic storm. The mothership herself is surrounded by seven freighter-sized space craft, themselves derelicts, and is twenty-times the size of Galactica. An expedition lead by Captain is sent to investigate the mothership. While onboard, Lieutenant experiences a vision where one of the carcasses turns into Apollo and tells him that he must have Starbuck's soul. Doctor Wilker is separated from the expedition, himself attacked () and possessed by a Somnian ().

The Dreadnaught (or Dirigible) is an airship or lighter-than-air aircraft that patrols the skies of the virtual world environment known as New Cap City. Outfitted with an array of weapons, the dirigible is seen as a real threat by gamers in New Cap City - including Tad "Heracles" Thorean, who warned Joseph Adama about its danger shortly before being derezzed himself . Carrying a number of assault vehicles, the dirigible is capable of launching vintage Vipers and autogyros to strafe the streets of New Cap City .

The term frame describes the "ribs" of a vessel or main lateral bulkheads within a ship. In the Colonial Fleet, frames refer to the ribs that form structural segments of a battlestar. These major structural bulkheads provide structural strength as well as serve as dividers within the vessel's interior space into airtight compartments. Frames form a damage control against hull breaches that could vent atmosphere, equipment or crew into space. Frames help contain decompression within small compartments or bays. Often when discussing areas of the ship, frame numbers are used to quickly define sections of a vessel. When is hit with a nuclear warhead in its first encounter with Cylons during the Fall of the Twelve Colonies, Galactica XO Saul Tigh informs Commander Adama of the extent of the fires burning within the severely damaged port flight pod by referencing what compartments were on fire by saying "everything forward of frame 250". Tigh is referring to the lateral bulkhead within the port side flight pod, number 250, or in other words the 250th lateral structural bulkhead support rib within the hull's superstructure .

The Fourth Fleet is made up of over 600 offensive-capable spacecraft. Led by Commander Kronus from the battlestar Rycon, the Fourth Fleet repelled a major Cylon offensive (destroying three basestars) at the Battle of Cosmora Archipelago. During that battle the Rycon fell, and the ships of the Fourth Fleet are presumed destroyed either prior to or during the Battle of Cimtar (Take the Celestra). de: Vierte Flotte

The Colonial Fleet does not appear to possess the ability to communicate faster than light, other than by sending a message on a ship making an FTL jump. The Cylons however, indicate a possible capability of FTL/instantaneous communication without sending a ship to carry the message. * When a humanoid Cylon body is killed, the mind of the Cylon downloads to a resurrection tank. For example, Boomer is shot on (Resistance), and downloads to , many light years distant . While it is possible that her conscious is transmitted to a nearby Resurrection Ship which then jumps to Caprica, this would require the Cylons to stay in the same star system as the Colonials. The resurrection of killed Cylon agents would take years if the signal had to cross interstellar space. * The Cylons have repeatedly tracked the Fleet from long distances. For example, the Olympic Carrier is able to signal the location of the Fleet to the Cylons very rapidly after a jump . Fos is the commanding officer of Tityus, a ship in the Caprican Armed Forces, during the Caprica-Sagittaron Conflict. Fos is killed at the Battle of Sagittaron Bellarias following Isak's tactical update, which executes the Divine Imperative leading to the (Battlestar Galactica: Cylon War 3).

Coordinates psionically divined by Countess Sephoni purported to be those of lead to the Colonial's introduction to the ' super basestar, a ship strong enough to eradicate . This marks the first encounter with the Cylons in two yahrens.
An escape pod is a small, one-man emergency vehicle housed within the SuperViper.
The foundry ship is a vessel within the Colonial fleet responsible for manufacturing new Viper models, such as the Twisters.

The Galleon Meadow is a location on where the thirteen tribes completed their respective journeys away from aboard a "great ship" called the "galleon," as written in the Sacred Scrolls. The meadow's exact location is known, and it is the nearest landmark on the path to the Tomb of Athena. From the Meadow one can see the High Road, a rocky ridge leading in the direction of the tomb. The Faction that sought the Tomb landed here from the Astral Queen following the cooperative Caprica copy of Cylon infiltrator Sharon Valerii on their journey .

The Gideon Massacre is a confrontation between Colonial Marines and Colonial civilians that took place on the heavy hauler Gideon, after the ship's crew refused to resupply following the forced removal of President Laura Roslin, dissolving of the Quorum of Twelve, and the declaration of martial law by Galactica executive officer, Saul Tigh .

The Galactica-type battlestar, erroneously known as a Jupiter-class in apocrypha works, is a Colonial capital ship that combines the functions of an aircraft carrier and a battleship. It was designed and deployed after the outbreak of hostilities between the and Colonials. A few ships of this class remain in service over 40 years after the end of the Cylon War; however, most were retired shortly after the War ended.

Gus is a crew member aboard Pegasus who works in the ship's galley with Kendra Shaw. Shaw mentions to him that "the more things change, the more things stay the same" after hearing 's first speech to Pegasus's crew, to which he, clearly displeased, replies in the affirmative .

The great powers are what Count Iblis claims destroyed his ship. When asked about them, Iblis is initially evasive, other than to scoff at the possibility of them being Cylons. When pressed by , Iblis reveals that "there are greater and more infinitely dangerous powers in the universe than your Cylons and all their allies combined." It is unknown whether the powers were in fact the Beings of Light or other forces .

The Graystone Blimp is a floating airship owned by Graystone Industries and the CapTV Network in Caprica City in the years prior to the Cylon War. CAP Sports Channel uses the Graystone Blimp to provide aerial coverage of Caprica City Buccaneers Pyramid games, shooting the action from high above Atlas Arena .

A gun camera is a camera used to automatically record images of the target when a Viper pilot's guns are fired. A Raptor has a gun camera with manual control ( tells Skulls to record the Resurrection Hub with the gun camera ("Guess What's Coming to Dinner")). IFF is an acronym for Identification Friend or Foe, a transponder-based system of spacecraft identification, used to distinguish friendly from enemy craft. The Cylon transponders found on Galactica contain IFF technology and are used by the crew in clandestine approaches to Cylon strongholds . Colonial civilian and military ships, such as s and Raptors, also have transponders. The civilian ships likely use civilian transponders used for commercial passenger flight, but are now recognized by Galactica as part of its Fleet. The Blackbird was likely not equipped with a transponder (or the transponder is disabled as part of its function), which almost leads to it being attacked by other Vipers whose pilots mistake its questionable DRADIS signature as a Cylon target after the stealth fighter returns from a reconnaissance mission .

The Imperium Class Raider is an upgrated variant of the Cylon Raider. The Imperium class ship is armed with four forward firing energy weapons instead of the normal two common to most Cylons ships (2003 Video Game).

The Cylon Heavy Tanker is a larger variant of the Cylon freighter with greater armor and a larger cargo capacity. Heavy Tankers carry volatile tylium for use in the Cylon war effort and is typically encountered in convoys with a fighter screen of Cylon Raiders (2003 Video Game).

Hillard is a member of Samuel Anders' resistance group on , and a former member of the Caprica Buccaneers pyramid team circa . He engages in high-altitude training with the Buccaneers during the Fall of the Twelve Colonies, summarily witnessing the nuclear bombardment from a distance, and later participating in guerrilla warfare against targets . As the Cylons restore various cities on Caprica, Hillard aids Anders and Jean Barolay in planting a bomb under a Cylon café in Delphi nine months later . Following the Resistance's rescue by 's search-and-rescue mission, Hillard integrates into , surviving New Caprica, and later taking part part in the harvesting mission on the algae planet as a civilian member of the marine detachment responsible for protecting the civilian workers. When the Cylons, searching to find entry into the nearby Temple of Five, come across them and attack, Hillard's mardet fends off the Centurion advance and is killed in the firefight . de: Hillard

The helm is the Colonial term for the helmet worn by pilots. It serves several functions, when worn it erects an energy shield that covers the opening in the face, in addition to the breach around the neck. On the inside of the shield, it offers a visual readout called an info-scroll, in addition to an internal communicator that allows communication to other ships and . It also serves as a filter and oxygen supply, capable of extracting oxygen from unbreathable atmospheres

While patrolling the flight corridors leading to Earth, Captain Kanon and Lieutenant Briton of Recon Probe Delta encounter an advanced Cylon craft. After engaging the ship in battle, and noting that the Cylons look humanoid, they determine that they must disable it before it reaches Earth. The pilots determine that the Viper cannot destroy the craft with firepower alone, since the Cyon ship is too fast and too well armed. Knowing that the ship's present course would bring it to Earth, Kanon has no choice but to ram the ship, which causes the ship to crash land on Earth. The crash results in the destruction of Andromidus, an advanced Cylon form that looks humanoid, and three Centurions .

Hammer is a callsign for a Viper pilot serving aboard the battlestar after the end of the Cylon War. When Galactica is boarded by the Annihilators, Hammer informs Cerberus and Ulysses fighter groups that Galactica been boarded, before Galactica weapons are used against one of the battlestars (Battlestar Galactica: Origins 6).
The hybrid missile carrier is a Cylon craft deployed in 7358. These carriers were in use during the Ambush by the Super Basestar, targeting the Fleet's tanker formations ().

's Harvester docked atop starboard flight pod ().]] The Harvester is the primary class of spacecraft built by the Okaati during the seventh-millennium. Harvesters of varying size are constructed to house the remnants of the Okaati civilization during their millennia-long exile within their own fugitive fleet. While christened as a nod to their agricultural roots, Harvesters serve as manufacturing, resource processing, and housing crafts for the Okaati people. An exemplification of Okaati engineering acumen, Harvester crafts feature the ability to carry any cargo and convert it over to whatever they need, including the creation of new Harvesters. New Harvesters are built in space as their fleet travels the Empyrean Expanse (). Harvesters are built for both hauling and speed, given the Okaati's parasitical nature and their need to avoid the Comitat's pursuit crafts. While armed with fixed forward-facing weapons, Harvesters use their adroit nature to avoid combat, and are able to both board via airlocks capable of connecting a wide variety of different space crafts and installations, as well as towing ships of great bulk at rapid speed via magnetic grapnels in concert with superior engine systems (-). illustrates how the Harvesters are central to their very existence, and their ability to make use of materials to build new ships for their fleet ().]]
Hyapatia is a battle cruiser serving in Commander Cain's Poseidon colony fleet.

Captain Kanon is a pilot on patrol with Lieutenant Briton when a specialized Raider appears. Unable to destroy the Raider, Kanon rams the enemy fighter with his Viper. While he disables the Raider, Briton is injured and their Viper is considered missing for some time until it manages to limp back to to warn them of the humanoid detected aboard the stricken Raider . de:Kanon

Jasper is an "old codger in his sixties" whose profession is that of an intergalactic prospector. With his ship, the Golden Queen, he and his pet simian, Nugget, discover the richest ore planetoid in the star system called Opelon. However, after discovering this, the Cylons lead by seize the asteroid, forcing Jasper to flee. After being rescued by , and , Jasper befriends , regaling him in tales of having seen the fabled colony of the Thirteenth Tribe, Earth (I Have Seen Earth).

John Zinman is a television writer and producer, and part of the writing staff and production team of the Re-imagined Series spin-off Caprica. Zinman and Patrick Massett produced such television shows as Veritas: The Quest and worked as Consulting Producer for both Friday Night Lights (which they were nominated in 2006 for a WGA Award) and Knight Rider. They also wrote the screenplay for the 2001 film Lara Croft: Tomb Raider.

Captain Jor is a Colonial scientist, who commands the agro ship Rhea before the destruction of the Colonies. He resides aboard the ship with wife and their son, Kel.

Janey is the wife of Viper pilot Jim Kirby and mother of their son Anslem circa . She believes her husband was killed in action when his ship, the battlestar Valkyrie, was reportedly destroyed near Canceron Prime. In reality, Kirby is alive but serving in the secret "ghost fleet" and officially listed as deceased by the Colonial Fleet. Janey lives on Picon as a single mother, unaware that her husband is still alive .
Launch tubes are specially designed airlocks used to quickly catapult s and other similar craft from their parent vessel and into space.

.]] The laser bola is a traditional weapon of the Borellian Nomen. Up to three are usually slung on bandoliers on Nomen, whose Code dictates that they never leave their person or be drawn in haste, without thought. When thrown, they appear as two glowing balls connected by a red laser line. Once drawn, however, they must be thrown at a target or explode upon reaching critical mass; they cannot be deactivated by any other means. Should the bola not be thrown at a target, the detonation time is around 50 to 60 microns after activation. Once discharged against a target, laser bola can be recovered and reused . de:Laserkugel

A landram is a tracked vehicle used for ground operations , typically shuttled to a planet via a shuttle . It is capable of holding crew and cargo, and is equipped with a top mounted turret weapon. A landram was used for the initial scouting of Carillon. They were later used to evacuate civilians and warriors from the "pleasure resort" on the planet . Such crafts are typically conveyed to planetoid surfaces via shuttles.

Linden is a resident on Prometheus. When attempts to find Phelan, Linden attempts to hustle Adama, who in turn attempts to find out where Phelan is on the ship. However, Linden remarks that this is "a very expensive question," for which Adama trades a pocket-sized picture holder (that Shevon gave Adama) for this information. Adama originally attempts to trade his sidearm for the information, but Linden remarks that they have guns. Linden accepts the picture holder because he "like[s] pretty things." After Adama has his information, Linden attempts to pawn off his newly acquired item for something (deleted scene, "Black Market").

Launch keys are a critical component aboard Colonial ships. They are used to start up a ship's power plant and engines. Their removal from a ship will immobilize it. During a briefing aboard the battlestar Galactica, senior officers learn that grounded civilian ships on New Caprica have had their launch keys removed by Cylons occupying the planet. The keys are very hard to duplicate, and Commander rules out making new ones as too difficult and time consuming . One of the resistance's goals is to recover them, which Lieutenant manages to do after landing covertly on the planet and infiltrating a secure storage facility . de:Startschlüssel

:This article discusses the fighter launch platforms of the Original Series battlestars. For information about similar facilities on Re-imagined Series battlestars, see launch tubes (RDM), landing bay and flight pod. The launch bay is a place from where a Colonial battlestar launches its s and other spacecraft. Battlestars have two launch bays enclosed within two quasi-cylindrical nacelles located port and starboard of the ship. One of the bays is known as "launch bay alpha" . The launch bays are directly adjacent to 16 launch tubes each, which are slanted towards the battlestar's aft. Designed solely for Viper craft, each of the sixteen launch tubes has a track in the launch bay where the Viper sits. An elevator provides access to the launch bay ("Saga of a Star World," "Lost Planet of the Gods, Part I"). In addition, a rapid transport trolley permits fast transportation from the pilots' quarters to the launch tubes when the ship goes on red alert .

A laser generator is the primary component of the 's laser weapon system. In order to make room for the second pulse generator for all of Starchaser engines, the laser generator is removed, thus removing the defensive capabilities of the Recon Viper .

A kilon is a measure of a starship's speed through space. A speed of 289 kilons is considered to be a cruising speed, seeing as an individual at 's briefing in the war room notes that such a speed would "seem to [indicate to said individual] that [the Cylons] are not in any kind of pursuit" ().

Leroy is an officer with the New York State Police who rides in car seven, unit 1711. He and his partner, Max, see the smoke plumes and explosions from the crash of the A-B Raider roughly 60 miles north of New York city. Upon arriving at the crash site, Leroy talks to their chief, who tells him to seal off the area. Max, just having been told this, tells Leroy to search the wreckage for drugs so they can get whatever credit they can. They later attempt to arrest Troy and Dillon on the suspicion that they are drug smugglers, but are subsequently stunned .

Leadfoot is the callsign of a pilot on Atlantia. Two years after the end of the Cylon War, he helps paint William Adama's Viper helmet as Adama makes his thousandth landing. When asked by his captain, Leadfoot notes that he is only 23 landings away from his thousandth (Battlestar Galactica: Origins 5).

Leslie Starus is a woman that lives on Aurora, a civilian ship in The Fleet. She made scarfs for people across the fleet. Emily Kowalski gave one to Laura Roslin during their time together on Galactica before Emily died .

The Cylon light tanker (or Cylon freighter) is an unarmed ship used throughout the Cylon sphere of influence to transport fuel and other goods. The tanker transports 8 cargo pods of Tylium deposits which are then taken to fuel refineries at spots throughout space. Each fuel pod can be ejected independently as an offensive measure. The light tanker is not very heavily armored as they are always escorted wherever they go (2003 Video Game).

Lingk is a Borellian Noman serving aboard the supply ship Broadside within the Fleet. He serves under Mega, the leader of the Borellian survivors, and becomes suspicious of the disguised Lucifer, whom he ultimately discovers to be an impostor.

The magnetic void is a space phenomenon which obscures stars and causes sensor malfunctions on ships. A ship can find itself easily lost within such a void due to these navigational hazards. A magnetic void was described in the Book of the Word during the exodus from . finds the story useful in finding the planet, where he hopes to learn more about the path of the Thirteenth Tribe .

Meier is one of Tom Zarek's right-hand men in Zarek's quest for political power in the Fleet. Meier warns Zarek of an unknown spacecraft approaching the Astral Queen while they and other ships of Roslin's faction orbit Kobol in search of the whereabouts of Earth. Meier suggests engaging it using the Adriatic weapons, one of the few civilian ships of the fleet that had defensive ability. Laura Roslin delays the attack until identifies herself as piloting the craft. Later, Meier and Zarek decides that the only way for Zarek to gain access to Roslin's inner circle (and later, with Roslin's death from illness, to rise to power) was for her most influential advisor, , to die. As it was said in the Sacred Scrolls that humans returning to Kobol face a deadly risk, Meier decides that this would be the perfect cover for Adama's death . On , Zarek warns Meier to be cautious and await the best opportunity. However, such an opportunity passes after Commander Adama's party arrived; Zarek tells Meier to cancel the operation. Meier ignores Zarek's order, continuing his plan by recruiting the future neé Valerii to assassinate Lee for them, leaving Zarek's hands effectively clean. Luxury liners are a series of popular passenger craft that are employed by various operators in the Twelve Colonies in the years before the Fall. There are at least two distinct types of liners defined by their fin placements: a flat-fin back (e.g. Olympic Carrier) and a front-fin (e.g. Colonial Heavy 798).

The Loki type heavy cruiser is a lightly armed support ship in service with the Colonial Fleet during the First Cylon War, where two or three of these ships would be assigned to a battlestar group at any given time. The ships are designed to receive goods and munitions, and transfer them to combat ships underway (Blood & Chrome).

Missile batteries, missile tubes, and missile launchers are weapon emplacements aboard Cylon and Colonial military ships capable of firing conventional or nuclear ship to ship, or ship to ground ordnance. They are protected against damage by retraction mechanisms on Cylon craft, and by external hatches on Colonial craft, and vary in size depending on the class of ship. Some missile launchers are even placed on planetary and other astral surfaces.

A metron bomb is a weapon used by the Cylons. In attempting to discover oddities in Specter's command of the Attila garrison, Lucifer discovers that Specter has ordered more of these weapons than any other garrison in the system .

Milo is a boy who works aboard Hitei Kan following the Second Exodus. Nearing the age of 12, he helps in sabotaging the refinery ship by hiding pressure relief seals vital to the processing equipment, which later turn up as a result of Cabott and Xeno Fenner's arrest .

Nixon Kinlow is a professional gun-for-hire who is recruited by the Labor Ministry to kill Karen Zarek of the Citizens for Sagittaron Labor Reform. After successfully assassinating the already-terminal Zarek in Sagittaron City , the Labor Ministry reneges on their deal with Kinlow and sends him off to Luna Three. Approximately 13 years prior to the Fall of the Colonies, Zarek discovers Kinlow working at the mining camp as well. Kinlow is forced to do Zarek's bidding, which involves killing off Jason Melton. After that deed is done, Zarek shoots him in the head to satisfy his revenge .

The Minerva-class light battlestar is a Colonial Fleet battleship in operation during the First Cylon War. Neptune is the 's crisis-control ship, operating under military service in . Neptune dispatches a shuttle with a crisis response crew to board the burning Hepahestus, only to be be besieged by seditionist elements and trapped aboard despite Boomer's assistance. Boomer is able to assist in extracting Neptune surviving crew during a battle, saving a bulk of their team .

Chief Nedder was a non-commissioned officer in the Colonial Fleet who served with William Adama on his first ship before the First Cylon War. He volunteered for duty aboard the Dreadnaught Invincible and was captured when the Cylons took control of the ship. For the next thirty years, Nedder was kept alive by the Cylons as the living, unwilling operator of Invincible. His body was dismantled and integrated with the ship's systems, with his living eye used to activate weapons and his handprint used to run the engines. This practice, a perversion of a human-designed failsafe, was the central "secret" of the Cylons, revealing their ultimate dependence on the enslavement of their former masters. When discovered by Adama, Nedder begs for death as a release from his torment. He is temporarily thwarted when Dr. Villem Fuest's self-sacrificing act to disable the ship is mistaken for an attack. After these events, the Cylons plan to "improve" Nedder by using "replacement parts" taken from captured human scavengers.

The OOD, or Officer of the Deck monitors the CIC's operation in the absence of the ship's commanding officer. The OOD generally carries out or relays the command officer's standing orders. In the absence of a command officer, the OOD has the conn, but typically calls the commanding officer before taking any action if time allows. Another term for the OOD is the watch officer. Aboard Galactica, this function is usually carried out on screen by Lieutenant Gaeta, the Senior Officer of the Watch.

Phaeton 5 is a ship in the Fleet. Phaeton was formerly a shipping barge of the Caprican Impex Corporation prior to the Fall of the Twelve Colonies. It has two hundred and fifty four survivors. A stowaway, a Returner by the name of Marco Lesa, and his daughter, Jenny, hide on this ship until he is severely injured by a murder attempt by the Earth Protectorate. Commander Adama and Dr. Sherman Cottle argue his fate .
Piscon is a freighter that survives the initial Cylon attack on the Twelve Colonies. Rifkus is slated to board this craft, but does not in fear of being killed by the Cylons .

Orestes is a transport vessel in the Fleet. The ship becomes the center of a crisis when an outbreak of Parahelial Fever occurs among the 42 children aboard. After its crew and passengers escape aboard a captured Cylon shuttle, Orestes is presumably left abandoned .

In the Re-imagined Series, propulsion systems are powered by fuel refined from tylium ore. A ship's primary propulsion systems, referred to as "sublight engines," allow it to travel at a slight fraction of the speed of light, which is sufficient to traverse the distances between planets in a solar system in relatively short timeframes. Most ships in the series also have a secondary system, called a faster-than-light drive (or "FTL"), that enables a ship to travel interstellar distances almost instantaneously, by "folding up space" in between the ship and its destination. Since, under normal circumstances, a ship that has used its FTL drive cannot be followed without explicit information about its destination, this technology is used extensively in strategic and tactical maneuvers.

Sperrin is the doctor aboard the transport Orestes. He manages the outbreak of Parahelial Fever among the children on his ship. When Apollo is taken aboard the Cylon basestar, he leaves Dr. Sperrin in command of Orestes .

Slug is a crewman aboard the supply ship Broadside under Captain Ironhand's command. He is described as "slump-shouldered" and "pot-bellied," with an extremely lethargic demeanor that epitomizes the ship's poor crew discipline. Slug serves as an unofficial greeter for new arrivals aboard Broadside, escorting them to Captain Ironhand's quarters for questioning. He also leads new crew members to their assigned quarters after acceptance by the captain. His performance of these duties is notably slow and unenthusiastic, moving at a pace described as "almost ritualistically lethargic." When leaving the captain's presence, he takes "forever to close the cabin door," which visibly disgusts Ironhand. Slug shows minimal interest in his surroundings or duties, demonstrating indifference even to direct criticism. When Baltar sarcastically remarks that his name "seems appropriate," Slug hears the comment but is "just not interested enough to think about it." His apathetic approach to security allows infiltrators like Baltar and Lucifer to gain access to the ship without proper scrutiny. Captain Ironhand's reaction to Slug reflects his broader frustration with Broadside crew, hoping that new arrivals will prove to be "better hands than that one" as crew members "did only as much work as they were told, and no more."

The Tharian spaceship is a massive, silent vessel that appears in the path of Galactica as it approaches the planet Thar. It does not respond to any communications and appears to be an inert, solid object. However, it is later revealed to be an illusion—a holographic image of a small model, extra-dimensionally projected into space and enlarged ten thousand times by the advanced Tharians. Before any Viper or Raptor can fire weapons at will, permission must be given for members of the fighter group to do so. The request or command is called "weapons free." The lead pilot of a Combat Air Patrol, or group of Alert Fighters (typically the CAG) can give a "weapons free" order when facing a known enemy. Any member of a fighter group can request weapons-free authorization from the lead pilot, usually as part of training missions or to verify their fighter's gun operation . In special cases, the lead pilot may defer weapons-free authorization to the battlestar commander. Lead pilot defers weapons-free authorization for her fighter group to Galactica Actual after the battlestar launches her fighters against sister battlestar Pegasus and her Vipers, realizing that ordering fire against fellow Colonials required Commander Adama's authorization . The contrary command to "Weapons Free" is "Weapons Hold", whereby units are ordered to hold fire except against specifically authorized targets or in self-defense. Under "Weapons Free", any target not known to be friendly may be engaged. Example: Assume pilot call sign Joker is flying CAP, led by pilot call sign Birdie. Joker is in pursuit of an enemy vessel and wishes to fire upon it. (Joker is under "weapons hold," therefore the safeties are engaged on his weaponry.) - Pilot: Birdie, Joker. Target in sight. A kinetic energy weapon is a weapon that causes damage as a result of the kinetic energy (motion) imparted to a projectile. This includes firearms firing solid bullets first and foremost but may also include guns firing explosive shells. In fan circles, the battlestar and Viper weapons are sometimes called railguns. However this has never been stated on screen and a lot of evidence, like the use of chemically propelled rounds, points to them being conventional guns. Indeed, the exact nature of these weapons is still being discussed by the production team (some like Gary Hutzel want them to be based on railgun technology, while some in the writing staff feel that they are not railguns) .
